2608.27442.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
2608.27442.paper_summary: In real-world software development, code review typically involves iterative interactions between developers and reviewers to improve software quality, making the process costly and time-consuming. Although recent work explores large language models (LLMs) for automated code review, most approaches oversimplify code review into a single-round, static decision task, which fails to capture the multi-round interactive nature and the complex problem-solving processes inherent in realistic review scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce MCR-Bench, the first defect state-aware benchmark designed for realistic multi-round code review. MCR-Bench covers five commonly-used programming languages and consists of 2,269 real-world multi-round code review tasks, each of which is annotated with fine-grained defect information and cross-round state labels. Each task in MCR-Bench is equipped with fine-grained defect metadata (e.g., description, type, severity) alongside dynamic state annotations, capturing the complete evolutionary trajectory of a defect throughout the multi-round process. We obtain several findings through extensive experiments on MCR-Bench with mainstream LLMs. (1) Limited overall capability: experiments reveal that mainstream LLMs exhibit limited overall performance in defect detection and defect lifecycle state tracking, with performance degrading significantly as the number of interaction rounds increases; (2) Defect-sensitive performance: LLMs' performance varies substantially across different defect types and severity levels, with semantically complex or low-salience defects being significantly more likely to be missed; (3) Underlying Failure Mechanisms: our in-depth error analysis dissects the distinct drivers of false positives and false negatives, revealing critical weaknesses such as cross-round temporal misalignment and inadequate long-range memory.
2608.27442.paper_summary_zh: 在現實世界的軟體開發中，代碼審查通常涉及開發者和審查者之間的反覆互動，以提高軟體質量，這使得過程成本高昂且耗時。儘管最近的研究探索了大型語言模型（LLMs）在自動化代碼審查中的應用，但大多數方法將代碼審查簡化為單輪的靜態決策任務，這無法捕捉到現實審查場景中固有的多輪互動特性和複雜的問題解決過程。為了填補這一空白，我們介紹了 MCR-Bench，這是首個針對現實多輪代碼審查設計的缺陷狀態感知基準。MCR-Bench 涵蓋五種常用的程式語言，並包含 2,269 個真實的多輪代碼審查任務，每個任務都附有細緻的缺陷資訊和跨輪狀態標籤。MCR-Bench 中的每個任務都配備了細緻的缺陷元數據（例如，描述、類型、嚴重性）以及動態狀態註解，捕捉缺陷在多輪過程中的完整演變軌跡。我們通過對 MCR-Bench 進行廣泛實驗，使用主流 LLMs 獲得了幾個發現。（1）整體能力有限：實驗顯示主流 LLMs 在缺陷檢測和缺陷生命周期狀態追蹤方面的整體性能有限，隨著互動輪次的增加，性能顯著下降；（2）缺陷敏感性性能：LLMs 的性能在不同的缺陷類型和嚴重性水平之間變化顯著，語義複雜或低顯著性的缺陷被漏檢的可能性顯著增加；（3）潛在失敗機制：我們的深入錯誤分析剖析了假陽性和假陰性的不同驅動因素，揭示了關鍵弱點，如跨輪時間錯位和不充分的長期記憶。
